zh: 船到杭州，王有龄回家歇得一歇，随即换了官服，去谒见抚台，当面禀报了此行的经过，同时呈上一封信：黄宗汉老家的回信，两万两银子业经妥收。这趟差使，公私两方面都办得极其漂亮，黄宗汉异常满意。“你辛苦了！我心里有数。”他说，“我自有打算，几天以内，就有信息。”“是！”王有龄不敢多问，辞出抚署，接着又去谒见藩司麟桂。麟桂对王有龄，因为顾忌着黄宗汉难惹的缘故，本来抱的是敬鬼神而远之的态度，好也罢，歹也罢，反正天塌下来有长人顶，自己不求有功，但求无过，凡事不生麻烦就够了。及至看他此行办得圆通周到，而且颇懂“规矩”，已觉喜出望外，加以有同委员替他吹嘘，越发刮目相看。等把手本一递进去，立即使传下话来：“请王大老爷换了便衣，在签押房相见。”这是接待地位仿佛而交情特深的朋友的方式，王有龄知道，是周委员替自己说了好话的效验，而收服了周委员，又是胡雪岩的功劳。想到他，再想到麟桂的优礼有加，顿时有了一个主意，要请麟桂来保荐胡雪岩。
en: When the boats reached Hangzhou, Wang rested briefly at home, changed into official robes, and went to see the governor. He personally reported the journey and presented a letter from Huang's family acknowledging safe receipt of the twenty thousand taels. Both the public and private aspects of the assignment had been handled handsomely. Huang was exceedingly pleased. “You've worked hard. I know what you've done,” he said. “I have plans of my own. You'll hear something within a few days.” “Yes, Your Excellency.” Wang dared not inquire further. Leaving the governor's yamen, he went to call on Treasurer Lingui. Knowing how difficult Huang could be, Lingui had previously treated Wang rather like a spirit best respected from a distance. Whether things went well or badly, someone taller would hold up the falling sky. He sought no merit, only freedom from blame and trouble. Now Wang's tactful, thorough handling of the journey, together with his understanding of the “rules,” had exceeded Lingui's hopes. Zhou's praise made him regard Wang more highly still. As soon as the visiting card went in, a message came out: “Ask His Honour Wang to change into ordinary clothes and meet me in my private office.” This was how one received an intimate friend of roughly equal standing. Wang knew that Zhou's favourable account had produced the result, and that Hu deserved the credit for winning Zhou over. Thinking of Hu and of Lingui's exceptional courtesy, he suddenly had an idea: he would ask Lingui to recommend Hu for advancement.

zh: 在签押房彼此以便眼相见，旗人多礼，麟桂拉着王有龄的手，从旅途顺适问到“府上安好”，这样亲热了一番，才把他让到西屋去坐。签押房是一座小院落，一明两暗三间平房，正中算是小客厅，东屋签押办公，西屋才是麟桂日常坐起之处，掀开门帘，就看见红木炕床上。摆着一副烟盘，一个长辫子，水蛇腰的丫头刚点起一盏明晃晃的“太谷灯”。“请！”麟桂指着炕床上首说。“大人自己请吧！”王有龄笑道，“我享不来这份福！”“不会也好。”麟桂不说客套说。“说实在的，这玩意儿益处少，害处多。不过，你不妨陪我躺一躺。”这倒无妨，能不上瘾。躺烟盘是件很有趣的事，而能够并头隔着荧荧一火说话，交情也就会不同。所以王有龄欣然应诺，在下首躺了下去。那个俏伶伶的丫头，马上走过来捧住他的脚，脱下靴子，拉一张方凳把他的双足搁好，接着拿床俄国毯子为他围住下半身。
en: They met in ordinary clothes in the private office. The Manchus were ceremonious, and Lingui took Wang's hand, asked whether the journey had gone smoothly and whether everyone at home was well, then, after these affectionate greetings, led him into the western room. The office occupied a small courtyard, with a single-storey building of three rooms: an open central reception room and an enclosed room on either side. Documents were signed and business conducted in the eastern room; the western was Lingui's everyday sitting room. As the curtain lifted, Wang saw an opium tray on a rosewood couch. A maid with a long plait and slender waist had just lit a bright Taigu lamp. “Please,” Lingui said, indicating the upper end of the couch. “You take it, Your Excellency.” Wang smiled. “I don't know how to enjoy that pleasure.” “It's just as well that you don't.” Lingui dispensed with polite pretence. “In truth, the stuff does more harm than good. But you can lie down and keep me company.” That was harmless enough. Provided one did not become addicted, conversation beside an opium tray could be entertaining, and lying head to head across the little flame could deepen a friendship. Wang readily agreed and reclined at the lower end. The pretty maid immediately held his feet, removed his boots, arranged a square stool beneath them, and covered his lower body with a Russian blanket.

zh: 另有个丫头已经端来了四个小小的果碟子，两把极精致的小茶壶。在烟盘上放好，随即使坐在小凳子上打烟。装好一筒，把那支镶翠的象牙烟枪往王有龄唇边送了过来。“请你们老爷抽。我不会。”麟桂当仁不让，一口气把烟抽完，拿起滚烫的茶壶喝了一口，再拈一粒松子糖塞在嘴里，然后慢慢从鼻孔喷着烟，闭上眼睛，显得飘飘欲仙似地。“雪轩兄！”麟桂开始谈到正事，“你这一趟，替浙江很挣了面子。公事都象老兄这么顺利，我就舒服了。”“这也全靠大人的荫庇。”王有龄说，“总要长官信任，属下才好放手去干。”“也要先放心，才好放手。说老实话，我对你老兄再放心不过，凡事有抚台在那里抗着，你怎么说怎么好。”麟桂又说，“抚台也是很精明的人，将心比心，一定也会照应我。”说了这一句，他抽第二筒，王有龄把他的话在心里琢磨了一阵，觉得他后半段话的言外之意，是要自己在伺候抚台以外，也别忘了该有他应得的一份。其实这话是用不着他说的，胡雪岩早就替他想到了。
en: Another maid brought four small dishes of fruit and two exquisite little teapots. Setting them beside the tray, she sat on a low stool to prepare the opium. Once a pipe was filled, she offered its jade-inlaid ivory stem to Wang's lips. “Give it to your master. I don't smoke.” Lingui accepted without ceremony, finished the pipe in one sustained breath, drank from the hot teapot, and put a pine-nut sweet into his mouth. Then, slowly letting smoke escape through his nostrils, he closed his eyes as though transported. “Brother Xuexuan,” he began, turning to business, “you've done Zhejiang great credit on this journey. If all official business went as smoothly as yours, I could live comfortably.” “It was entirely due to Your Excellency's support. Subordinates can act freely only when their superiors trust them.” “One must first feel secure before allowing a free hand. Frankly, I couldn't feel more secure about you. With the governor standing behind everything, whatever you propose is acceptable.” Lingui added, “The governor is a shrewd man too. If he puts himself in my position, he's certain to look after me.” He smoked a second pipe. Wang considered his words and concluded that the latter remark meant he must not forget Lingui's proper share while attending to the governor. In fact, there was no need to say it: Hu had already thought of that.

zh: 不过王有龄做官，已学得一个决窍，不有为外人所知的事，必须要做得密不通风，所以虽然一榻相对，只因为有个打烟的丫头在，他亦不肯有所表示。“说得是。”王有龄这样答道：“做事要遇着两种长官，最好当然是象大人这样，仁厚宽大，体恤部属，不得已而求其次，倒宁愿在黄抚台手下，虽然精明，到底好歹是非是极分明的。”“知道好歹是不错，说‘是非分明’，只怕不见得。‘麟桂说了这话，却又后悔，”雪轩兄。“他故意说反话，”这些话，你得便不妨在抚台面前提一提。“王有龄也极机警，“这可敬谢不敏了！”他笔着回答，“我从不爱在人背后传话。无端生出多少是非，于人有损，于己无益，何苦来哉！”麟桂对他这个表示。印象深刻，心里便想：此人确是八面玲珑，可以放心。
en: But Wang had learned one principle of official life: anything not meant for outsiders' knowledge must be kept completely secret. Though they faced each other on the same couch, the presence of the maid preparing the pipe prevented him from making any sign. “Quite so,” he answered. “There are two sorts of superior one hopes to serve. The best is naturally someone like Your Excellency, generous, tolerant, and considerate of his subordinates. Failing that, I would prefer Governor Huang. Shrewd though he is, he certainly knows merit from fault and right from wrong.” “Merit from fault, perhaps. Right from wrong—not necessarily.” Lingui regretted the remark as soon as he made it. “Brother Xuexuan,” he added with deliberate irony, “you might mention these words to the governor when you have a chance.” Wang was quick to respond. “That is an honour I must decline!” he said with a smile. “I never care to carry tales behind people's backs. It causes needless trouble, harms others, and benefits oneself not at all. Why do it?” The answer impressed Lingui deeply. This man truly knew how to handle every situation. He could be trusted.

zh: 由于心理上的戒备已彻底解除，谈话无所顾忌，兴致也就越发好了。你谈到京里的许多情形，六部的规矩“则例”，让王有龄长了许多见识。最后又谈到公事，“今年新漕，还要上紧。江浙的赋额独重，而浙江实在不比江苏。杭、嘉、湖哪里比得上苏、松、太？杭、嘉、湖三府又以湖州为王，偏偏湖州的公事最难办。”麟桂叹口气说：“湖州府误漕撤任，一时竟找不着人去接手。真叫人头疼！”椿寿一条命就送在湖州，麟桂对此不能不具戒心。王有龄知道其中的症结，但谈下去怕谈到椿寿那一案，诸多未便，所以他只作倾听的样子，没有接口。“我倒有个主意！”麟桂忽然冒出来这么一句，却又沉吟不语，好半天才自问自答地说：“不行！办不通，没有这个规矩。”也不知他说的什么？王有龄百思不解，可也不便去问。就这冷场的片刻，麟桂二十四筒鸦片烟抽完，吩咐开饭。丫头退了出去传话，眼前别无他人，可以把那样东西拿出来了。
en: With his last psychological guard removed, Lingui spoke without reserve and with increasing pleasure. He discussed conditions in the capital and the rules and precedents of the six ministries, greatly enlarging Wang's knowledge. Finally he returned to official business. “We must press ahead with this year's new grain. Jiangsu and Zhejiang bear exceptionally heavy tax quotas, yet Zhejiang is really no match for Jiangsu. How can Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou compare with Suzhou, Songjiang, and Taicang? Of our three prefectures, Huzhou is the richest, but its affairs are the hardest to manage.” He sighed. “The prefect of Huzhou has been dismissed for delaying the grain, and for the moment I can't find anyone to take over. A real headache!” Chunshou had lost his life over Huzhou, so Lingui could not help being wary. Wang understood the difficulty, but feared that pursuing it would lead to Chunshou's case and all its awkward implications. He merely listened. “I do have an idea!” Lingui suddenly exclaimed, then fell silent. After a long pause, he answered himself. “No. It won't work. There's no precedent.” Wang could not imagine what he meant, but it was not his place to ask. During the ensuing silence, Lingui finished his twenty-fourth pipe and ordered dinner. The maids went out to pass on the instruction. With nobody else present, Wang could produce what he had brought.

zh: “我替大人带了个小玩意来！”王有龄一面说，一面从贴身衣袋里取出个纸包，隔着烟灯，递了过去。打开一看，是个极精致的皮夹子，皮质极软，看那花纹就知道是西洋来的，麟桂把玩了外表，要打开看看里面时，王有龄又开口了。“回头再打开吧！”显然的，其中别有花样，麟桂笑一笑说声：“多谢！”随即把皮夹了揣在身上。等开饭时，托故走了出去，悄悄启视，皮夹子里是一张五千两的银票。王有龄做得极秘密，麟桂却不避他的底下人，走进来肃客入座，第一句就说：“受惠甚多！粮道那里怎么样？”“也有些点缀。”“多少？”“三数。”这是说粮道那里送了三千两。麟桂点点头，又问：“送去了？”“还没有。”王有龄答道，“我自然要先来见了大人，再去拜他。”“今天是来不及了，明天早些去吧！他在这上面看得很重。”
en: “I've brought Your Excellency a little curiosity.” From an inner pocket he took a paper parcel and passed it across the opium lamp. Inside was an exquisite wallet of exceptionally soft leather. Its pattern immediately showed that it came from the West. Lingui examined the outside and was about to open it when Wang spoke again. “Perhaps later.” Plainly there was something special within. Lingui smiled, thanked him, and put it away. When dinner was served, he excused himself, slipped outside, and opened it privately. The wallet held a bank draft for five thousand taels. Wang had acted in great secrecy, but Lingui showed no concern about his servants. Returning to invite his guest to the table, his first words were, “I am much indebted to you. What about the grain intendant?” “A little something for him too.” “How much?” “Three.” He meant three thousand taels. Lingui nodded. “Delivered already?” “Not yet. Naturally, I had to call on Your Excellency before visiting him.” “It's too late today. Go early tomorrow. He takes these matters very seriously.”

zh: 这完全自己人关爱的口吻，王有龄觉得麟桂对自己的态度又进了一层，便以感激的声音答道：“多谢大人指点。”“把‘大人’两个字收起来行不行？”麟桂放下酒杯，皱着眉说，“俗不可耐，败人的酒兴。”王有龄微笑着答说：“恭敬不如从命，我敬称‘麟公’。请干一杯！”“好，好！”麟桂欣然引杯，随即又说：“我刚才的话还没有完。他可晓得粮道有个癖好？”“噢。我倒不知道，得要请教麟公。”“其实这癖好，人人都有，只以此公特甚。”麟桂笑道，“他好的是‘男儿膝下’！”王有龄愣住了，不知道他打的是什么哑谜？“足下才大如海，怎么这句歇后语就把你难住了？”原来如此？俗语说：“男儿膝下有黄金”，隐下的是“黄金”二字。旗人掉书袋，有时不伦不类，王有龄倒真的好笑了。
en: The tone was that of affectionate advice to one of his own people. Wang felt that their relationship had advanced another step. “Thank you for the guidance, Your Excellency,” he answered gratefully. “Could you put away that ‘Your Excellency’?” Lingui set down his wine cup and frowned. “It's unbearably commonplace and spoils the pleasure of drinking.” Wang smiled. “Obedience is better than ceremony. I shall call you Mr Lin, with every respect. Let us drink a cup!” “Excellent!” Lingui drank gladly, then continued, “I hadn't finished what I was saying. Do you know the grain intendant's particular passion?” “No. I must ask you to enlighten me.” “In fact, everyone shares it, but his case is exceptional.” Lingui smiled. “He loves what lies beneath a man's knees.” Wang was baffled by the riddle. “Your learning is as broad as the sea. Can this unfinished proverb defeat you?” So that was it! The saying ran, “There is gold beneath a man's knees.” The unspoken words were “there is gold.” The Manchus' attempts at literary wit could sometimes be oddly contrived. Wang was genuinely amused.

zh: “所以我劝我不必送银票，兑换了金叶子送去。”麟桂是说笑话的神精，有着忍俊不禁的愉悦，“听说此人每天临睡以前，以数金叶子为快，否则忽忽如有所失，一夜不能安枕。”“这倒是怪癖！”王有龄问道，“如果出远门怎么办呢？也带着金叶子上路？岂非慢藏海盗？“那就不知道了。”讲过笑话，又谈正题，麟桂问起上海官场的情形，王有龄把倪良耀的委屈和牢骚，以及答应照料他的眷属的话，都告诉了麟桂。“这件事我不好说什么！”麟桂这样回答：“甚至倪某的眷属，我也不便去管。我知道，抚台的疑心病很重。”
en: “So I advise you not to send a bank draft. Exchange it for gold leaf.” Lingui could scarcely suppress his amusement. “They say he delights in counting his gold sheets every night before bed. Otherwise he feels something is missing and cannot sleep peacefully.” “That is a curious habit. What happens when he travels?” Wang asked. “Does he take the gold with him? Wouldn't that invite thieves?” “That I don't know.” Their joking over, they returned to business. Lingui asked about official circles in Shanghai. Wang told him of Ni's grievances and complaints and his own promise to look after Ni's family. “I can say nothing about that,” Lingui replied. “I can't even concern myself with Ni's family. I know how suspicious the governor is.”

zh: “是的。”“所以我劝你，就是照料倪良耀的眷属，也只好偷偷摸摸，别让抚台知道。”麟桂放低了声音又说，“我实在不明白，我们这位黄大人何以如此刻薄？江苏藩司与浙江巡抚何干？把人折腾得那个样子？还有件事，更不应该……”麟桂说到紧要关头，忽然住口，这自然是因为这句话关系甚重，碍着王有龄是黄宗汉的红人，还有些不放心的缘故。了解到这一点，王有龄便不如追问，举杯相敬，心里思索着如何把话题扯了开去？麟桂倒觉得不好意思了，“跟你说了吧！”他说，“他有件损人利己的事，利己应该，损人就要看一看，伤了自己的同年，未免太不厚道。”黄宗汉是伤了哪一个同年？他们这一科的飞黄腾达，全靠同年能和衷共济，互相照应。黄宗汉本人，不也靠大军机彭蕴章和何桂清这两个同年替他斡旋掩遮，逼死藩司椿寿一案，才得安然无事？因此，王有龄对麟桂所说的话，有些将信将疑。
en: “Yes.” “So I advise you to look after them discreetly and keep it from the governor.” Lingui lowered his voice. “I truly don't understand why our Mr Huang is so harsh. What has the treasurer of Jiangsu to do with the governor of Zhejiang? Why torment him like that? And there's something else, even less defensible...” At the crucial point he stopped. Plainly the matter was important enough that Wang's status as Huang's favourite still troubled him. Understanding this, Wang thought it better not to press. He raised his cup and considered how to change the subject. Lingui, however, felt embarrassed. “I may as well tell you. He's done something to benefit himself at another man's expense. Looking after oneself is natural enough, but one ought to consider whom one harms. To injure a man from one's own examination cohort is hardly generous.” Which fellow graduate had Huang injured? Their cohort's remarkable advancement depended upon mutual support. Had Huang himself not relied upon Grand Councillor Peng Yunzhang and He Guiqing to intercede and shield him in the case of Chunshou's forced suicide? Wang therefore half doubted Lingui's story.

zh: “前些日子有道关于江浙防务的上谕，”麟桂问道，“不知你看到了没有？”“没有。”王有龄说，“我人在上海，好久未见邸抄了。”“那道上谕是这么说，‘浙江巡抚黄宗汉奏陈，拨兵赴江苏，并防堵浙省情形。’得旨：”甚妥！现今军务，汝若有见到之处，即行具奏。不必分彼此之见。‘“听他念完这道上谕，王有龄又惊又喜，派兵出省击敌，本是他的建议，原来黄宗汉竟已采纳，更想不到竟蒙天语褒奖！也因为如此，他要辩护：“拨兵出省，似乎也没有什么不对。”“对呀！没有人说不对。只是你做浙江的官，管浙江的事好了，上谕虽有‘不必分彼此之见’的话，我们自己要有分寸，不可越俎代庖。黄抚台却不问青红皂白，左一个折子、右一个折子，说江苏的军务，该如何如何部署，请问，”麟桂凑身向前，“叫你老哥，做了江苏巡抚，心里作何感想？”王有龄这才明白，黄宗汉为了自己的“圣眷”，不为他的同年江苏巡抚许乃钊留作地，这实在说不过去。而且他这样搞法，似乎是企图调任江苏。果然如此，更为不智，江苏诚然是海内膏腴之地，但一打仗就不好了。遇到机会，倒要劝劝他。
en: “There was an edict recently about the defence of Jiangsu and Zhejiang,” Lingui asked. “Did you see it?” “No. I was in Shanghai and haven't read the court bulletins for some time.” “It said: ‘Governor Huang Zonghan of Zhejiang reports the dispatch of troops to Jiangsu and arrangements for preventing an incursion into Zhejiang.’ The imperial response was: ‘Excellent. In the present military affairs, submit any useful observations you may have without distinguishing between the concerns of one province and another.’” Wang listened with surprise and delight. Sending troops beyond the provincial boundary to meet the enemy had been his suggestion. Huang had adopted it—and, more unexpectedly, received imperial praise! He therefore felt bound to defend it. “There seems nothing wrong with sending troops beyond the province.” “Indeed! Nobody says there is. But an official of Zhejiang should attend to Zhejiang's affairs. Even if the edict says not to distinguish between provinces, we must observe proper limits and not take over another man's duties. Yet Governor Huang sends memorial after memorial, indiscriminately telling the throne how Jiangsu's military affairs should be arranged. Tell me,” Lingui leaned forward, “if you were governor of Jiangsu, how would you feel?” Now Wang understood. For the sake of imperial favour, Huang was leaving no room for his fellow graduate Xu Naizhao, governor of Jiangsu. That was indefensible. His conduct also suggested an ambition to be transferred there. If so, it was still less wise. Jiangsu was certainly one of the empire's richest regions, but war made it an undesirable posting. If an opportunity arose, Wang ought to advise him against it.

zh: 麟桂不知他心中另有想法，见他不即开口，当他不以为然，便但率问道：“雪轩兄。你觉得我的话如何？”王有龄这才醒悟，怕引起误会，赶紧答道：“大人存心忠厚，所持的自然是正论。只是我人微言轻，不然倒要相机规谏。”“不必，不必！”麟桂摇着手说，“这是我把你老哥当作好朋友，说的知心话。不必让第三个人知道。”“那当然。”王有龄郑重表示。“大人所说的话，我一句不敢外泄。不过既见于明发上谕，就是我跟抚台说了，他也不会疑心到别人头上的。”“那倒随你。”麟桂又说，“许家虽是杭州巨室，与我并无干涉，我也不过就事论事，说一句公道话而已。”这个话题就此抛开，酒已差不多了。王有龄请主人“赏饭”，吃完随即告辞，麟桂知道他行装甫卸，家里还有许多事，也不留他，亲自送到中门，尽欢而散。
en: Unaware of these further thoughts, Lingui mistook Wang's silence for disagreement. He asked frankly, “Brother Xuexuan, what do you think of what I've said?” Wang came to himself and hurried to prevent a misunderstanding. “Your Excellency's intentions are generous, and your view is naturally just. Unfortunately, my position is too insignificant for my words to carry weight. Otherwise I would find an opportunity to advise him.” “No need!” Lingui waved his hands. “I'm speaking in confidence because I regard you as a good friend. Nobody else need hear of it.” “Of course.” Wang was solemn. “I wouldn't dare repeat a word of what you've said. But since the matter appears in a publicly issued edict, even if I spoke to the governor, he would have no reason to suspect anyone else.” “That is up to you. The Xu family is prominent in Hangzhou, but has no connection with me. I'm merely judging the matter and speaking fairly.” The subject was dropped. They had drunk enough, so Wang asked his host for rice, ate, and took his leave. Knowing that he had only just returned and must have much to do at home, Lingui did not detain him. He personally escorted him to the middle gate, and they parted in good spirits.

zh: 第二天又拜了一天客，凡是稍有交情的，无下有“土仪”馈赠，从上海来，所谓“土仪”实在是洋货。海禁初开，西洋的东西，在它本国不值钱，一到了中华，便视为奇珍，哪怕一方麻纱手帕，受者无不另眼相看。因此，这趟客拜下来，王有龄的人缘又结了不少。到晚回家，胡雪岩正在客厅里，逗着王有龄的小儿子说笑。不过一天不见，王有龄便如遇见多年不晤的知交一般，心里觉得有好些话，亟待倾吐。“你吃了饭没有？”他问。“没有。”胡雪岩说，“我原意想邀雪公到城隍山上去吃油蓑饼，现在天晚了，不行了。”王有龄对这个提议，深感光趣，“不晚！”他说，“快夏至了，白天正长，而且天也暖和，就晚了也不要紧。怎么走法？”“总不能鸣锣喝道而去吧！”胡雪岩笑着说。王有龄也自觉好笑，“当然换了便衣去。”他说，“我的意思是连轿子也不必坐，也不必带人，就安步当车走了去。”“那也好。戴上一副墨晶眼镜，遇见熟人也可不必招呼。”于是王有龄换上一件宝蓝缎袍，套一件玄色贡缎背心，竹布袜、双梁鞋，戴上墨晶大眼镜，捏了一把折扇，与胡雪岩两个人潇潇洒洒地，取道大井巷，直上城隍山。
en: Wang spent the following day making more calls, bringing gifts to everyone with whom he had even a slight acquaintance. Coming from Shanghai, these “local products” were in fact foreign goods. Maritime trade had only recently opened. Objects worth little in their Western countries became rare treasures in China. Even a linen handkerchief won unusual appreciation. The round of visits therefore gained Wang many more friends. When he returned home that evening, Hu was in the reception room, joking with his young son. They had been apart for only a day, yet Wang felt as though meeting an old friend after years of separation, with a great deal he urgently wished to say. “Have you eaten?” “No. I meant to invite you up City God Hill for yousuobing cakes, but it's too late now.” The suggestion appealed to Wang. “Not too late! The summer solstice is approaching, the days are long, and the weather is warm. Even if it gets late, it doesn't matter. How shall we go?” “Surely not with gongs and cries to clear the road!” Hu laughed. Wang was amused too. “Naturally, I'll change into ordinary clothes. I meant that we needn't even take a chair or servants. We can walk.” “Good. Put on dark crystal spectacles, and you needn't greet acquaintances if we meet any.” Wang changed into a sapphire-blue satin robe with a dark tribute-satin waistcoat, light cotton socks, and double-ridged shoes. Wearing his large dark spectacles and carrying a folding fan, he walked with Hu through Dajing Lane and straight up City God Hill, both looking at ease.

zh: “还是我们第一次见的那地方喝茶吧！”他说，“君子不忘本，今天好好照顾他一下。”这个“他”，自是指那个茶座的老板。这是他距胡雪岩第二次来，但处境与心境与第一次有天渊之别。一坐下来，四面眺望、神闲气静，一年不到的工夫，自是湖山不改，但他看出去仿佛改过了，“西子”格外绰约，青山格外妩媚。“两位吃酒、吃茶？”老板看他们的气派、服饰，不敢怠慢，亲自走来招呼。“茶也要，酒也要。”王有龄学着杭州腔说：“新茶上市了，你说说看，有点儿啥个好茶叶？”“太贵重的，不敢顶备，要去现买。”“现买就不必了。”王有龄想了好久说：“来壶菊花。”那茶座老板看王有龄有些奇怪，先问好茶叶，弄到头来喝壶菊花，看起来是个说大话，用小钱的角色。
en: “Let's have tea where we first met,” Wang said. “A gentleman doesn't forget his beginnings. We ought to give him some good custom today.” By “him,” he meant the proprietor of the tea place. This was Wang's second visit with Hu, but his circumstances and state of mind were worlds apart from the first. Once seated, he looked about calmly and contentedly. Less than a year had passed; the lake and hills were unchanged, yet to his eyes they seemed transformed. West Lake, the beautiful Xizi, looked more graceful, and the green hills more charming. “Wine or tea, gentlemen?” Their bearing and clothes made the proprietor unwilling to neglect them, and he came himself. “Both.” Wang imitated the Hangzhou accent. “The new tea is on sale. Tell us what good leaves you have.” “I don't dare keep anything too costly in stock. I'd have to buy it specially.” “No need for that.” After thinking for a long time, Wang said, “Bring a pot of chrysanthemum tea.” The proprietor found him odd. He had begun by asking for fine tea and ended with chrysanthemums. Apparently he was a man of grand words and small expenditure.

zh: 不但他诧异，胡雪岩也是如此，问道：“怎么喝菊花？”“我想了半天才想起来，去年就是喝的菊花。”这话只有胡雪岩心里明白，回首前尘，不免也有些感慨，不过他一向是只朝前看，不暇后顾的性情，所以旋即抛开往事，管自己点菜：“一鸡三吃，醋鱼‘带鬓’，有没有活鲫鱼，斤把重的？”“我到山下去弄一条。是不是做汤？”“对，奶汤鲫鱼，烫两碗竹叶青，弄四个小碟子。带几张油蓑饼，先吃起来。”“好的，马上就来。”等把茶泡了来，王有龄端杯在手，望着暗青淡紫的暮霭，追想去年在此地的光景，忽然感情激动了。“雪岩！”他用非常有劲道的声音说，“我们两个人合在一起，何事不可为？真要好好干一下。”“我也这么想，”胡雪岩说，“今天来就想跟你谈这件事。”
en: Hu too was surprised. “Why chrysanthemum?” “It took me a while to remember. That's what I drank last year.” Only Hu understood. The recollection stirred him as well, but his nature was to look ahead, with little time for the past. He quickly set it aside and ordered the meal. “One chicken prepared three ways; vinegar fish prepared daibin. Do you have a live crucian carp, about a jin in weight?” “I can get one from below the hill. For soup?” “Yes, crucian carp in milky broth. Warm two bowls of Zhuyeqing, bring four small dishes and a few yousuobing cakes, and we'll begin.” “Certainly. They'll be here at once.” When the tea arrived, Wang held his cup and gazed at the dark blue-green and pale purple of the evening haze. Remembering his circumstances here the previous year, he was suddenly overcome by feeling. “Xueyan,” he said with great force, “with the two of us together, what couldn't we accomplish? We must really make something of it.” “That's my thought too. It's what I came to discuss with you today.”

zh: “你说，你说！”“我想仍旧要干老本行。”“不是回信和吧？”王有龄半开玩笑地，说实在话，他还真怕信和的东家把胡雪岩请了回去。“我早已说过了，一不做‘回汤豆腐’，二是自己立个门户。”胡雪岩说，“现在因为打仗的关系，银价常常有上落，只要眼光准，兑进兑出，两面好嫌，机会不可惜过。”王有龄不响，箸下如雨，只管吃那一碟发芽豆。胡雪岩知道，不是他喜爱此物，而是心里有所盘算。盘算的当然是资本，其实不必他费心思，资本从哪里来？他早就筹划好了，不过自己不便先开口而已。那一个终于开口了：“雪岩！”说句老买话，我现在不原意你去开钱庄。目前是要你帮我，帮我也等于帮你自己。你好不好捐个功名，到哪里跟我在一起，抚台已经有话了，最近还有别样安排，大概总是再派我兼一个差，那时我越加要帮手，你总不能看着我顾此失彼，袖手不问吧？““这我早就想到了。开钱庄归开钱庄，帮你归帮你，我两样都照顾得来，你请放心好了。”“当然，你的本事我是再清楚不过，不会不放心……”
en: “Tell me!” “I still want to return to my old trade.” “Not to Xinhe, I hope?” Wang was half joking. In truth, he did fear that Xinhe's proprietor might persuade Hu to return. “I've already said it: I won't be bean curd warmed over in the same broth, and I mean to set up for myself. With the war, silver prices are constantly moving. With sound judgement, one can profit on both buying and selling. We mustn't miss the opportunity.” Wang said nothing. His chopsticks moved incessantly over a dish of sprouted beans. Hu knew it was not fondness for the dish: he was calculating. Naturally, he was thinking about capital. There was no need, for Hu had already planned where it would come from. But he could not conveniently say so first. Wang eventually spoke. “Xueyan, frankly, I don't want you opening a bank just now. I need your help, and helping me means helping yourself. Couldn't you purchase an official qualification and stay with me wherever I go? The governor has already spoken of another arrangement shortly. Presumably he'll give me an additional assignment, and then I'll need help all the more. You can't stand aside and watch me neglect one thing while attending to another.” “I've thought of that already. Opening a bank is one matter, helping you another. I can manage both. Rest assured.” “Of course. Nobody knows your ability better than I. Naturally I trust you...”

zh: 看到他口不应心，依旧不以为然的神情，胡雪岩便放低了声音说：“雪公，你现在刚刚得意，但说句老实话，外面还不大晓得，所以此刻我来开钱庄，才是机会。等到浙江官商两方面，人人都晓得有个王大老爷，人人都晓得你我的关系，那时我出面开钱庄，外面会怎么说？““无非说我出的本钱！你我的交情，不必瞒人，我出本钱让你开钱庄，也普通的紧。”“这话不错！不过，雪公，‘不招人妒是庸才’，可以不招妒而自己做得招妒，那就太傻了。到时候人家会说你动用公款，营商自肥，有人开玩笑，告你一状，叫我于心何安？”这话打动了王有龄的心，觉得不可不顾虑，因而有些踌躇了。“做事要做得不落痕迹。”胡雪岩的声音越低。“钱庄有一项好处，代理道库、县库，公家的银子没有利息，等于白借本钱。雪公，你迟早要放出去的，等你放出去再来现开一家钱庄，代理你那个州县的公库，痕迹就太明显了。所以我要抢在这时候开。这一说，你懂了吧？”“啊！”王有龄的感想不同了，“我懂了。”
en: Seeing that his words did not match his continuing reluctance, Hu lowered his voice. “You've only just begun to succeed, Mr Xuexuan. Frankly, people outside don't yet know much about you. That's precisely why this is the moment for me to open a bank. Once every official and merchant in Zhejiang knows His Honour Wang, and everyone knows our relationship, what will they say if I open one then?” “Only that I supplied the capital. There's no need to conceal our friendship. My financing a bank for you would be perfectly ordinary.” “True. But as the saying goes, only a mediocre man never arouses envy. If we could avoid it and deliberately invite it instead, we'd be foolish. People would say you were using public money for private profit. Someone might amuse himself by filing an accusation against you. How could I feel at ease then?” This struck home. Wang felt the danger could not be ignored and hesitated. “Things must be done without leaving obvious traces.” Hu spoke still more quietly. “A bank has one particular advantage: it can act for circuit and county treasuries. Public funds bear no interest, so they're effectively capital borrowed for nothing. Sooner or later you'll receive a local appointment. If I open a bank then and immediately take over your treasury's business, the connection will be too obvious. That's why I must act now. Do you understand?” “Ah!” Wang saw the matter differently. “I understand.”

zh: “只怕你还没有完全懂得其中的奥妙。‘隔行如隔山’， 我来讲给你听。”胡雪岩的计划是，好歹先立起一个门户来，外面要弄得热闹，其实是虚好的，内里是空的，等王有龄一旦放了州县，这家钱庄代理它的公库，解省的公款，源源而来，空就变成实的的了。“妙！”王有龄大笑，学着杭州话说：“雪岩，你真会变戏法儿！”“戏法总是假的，偶尔变一两套可以，变多了就不值钱了，值钱的还是有真东西拿出来。”“这倒在实实在在的话。”王有龄收敛笑容，正色说道：“我们商量起来，先说要多少资本？”
en: “Perhaps not all the subtleties yet. Different trades are separated as though by mountains. Let me explain.” Hu's plan was to establish a firm first, however modest its resources. Outwardly it must look busy and prosperous; inwardly it would have little substance. Once Wang was appointed to a department or county, the bank would handle its treasury business. Public funds being remitted to the provincial capital would flow in continuously, turning appearance into reality. “Brilliant!” Wang laughed and imitated the Hangzhou accent. “Xueyan, you really know how to perform conjuring tricks!” “A trick is still an illusion. One or two may be useful; too many lose their value. What matters is eventually producing something real.” “That's sound sense.” Wang stopped laughing and spoke seriously. “Let us plan it. First, how much capital is needed?”

zh: 于是两个人喝着酒，商议开钱庄的计划。主要的是筹划资本的来源，这可要先算“民折官办”的一盘帐，胡雪岩的记忆过人，心算又快，一笔笔算下来，要亏空一万四千多两银子，都记在信和的帐上。得了海运局这么一个好差使，没有弄到好处，反闹了一笔亏空，好象说不过去。但王有龄不以为意，这算是下的本钱，以这两个多月的成绩和各方面的关系来说，收获已多。只是有了亏空，还要筹措钱庄的本钱，他觉得有些为难。“本钱号称二十万，算它实收四分之一，也还要五万，眼前怕有些吃力！”“用不着五万。”胡雪岩说，“至多二万就行了。眼前先要弄几千银子，好把场面撑起来。”“几千两银子，随时都有。我马上拨给你。”“那就行了。”胡雪岩说，“藩台衙门那里有几万银子的差额好顿，本来要付给通裕的，现在不妨压一压。”“对，对！”王有龄想通了，“通裕已经借了十万，我们暗底下替他做了保人，这笔款子压一压也不是说不过去的事。”“正就是这话。不过这笔款子要领下来，总要好几个月的工夫，得要走走路子。”
en: Over wine, they discussed opening the bank. The main question was the source of capital, which first required a reckoning of the official-procurement affair. Hu had an extraordinary memory and calculated rapidly in his head. Item by item, the account came to a deficit of more than fourteen thousand taels, all entered in Xinhe's books. To obtain so desirable an assignment at the Sea Transport Bureau, gain nothing from it, and instead incur a deficit seemed hard to justify. Wang, however, did not mind. It was an investment. Judged by the achievements of the past two months and the connections established on every side, the return was already considerable. Yet finding capital for a bank on top of this debt seemed difficult. “If we announce capital of two hundred thousand taels, even a quarter actually paid in means fifty thousand. That may be a strain just now.” “We don't need fifty thousand,” Hu said. “Twenty thousand at most. For the moment, we need a few thousand to establish a proper appearance.” “A few thousand is available at any time. I'll transfer it to you at once.” “Then we're set. There's also a price-difference allowance of several tens of thousands to draw from the provincial treasury. It was meant for Tongyu, but we can hold it back for a while.” “Yes!” Wang saw the point. “Tongyu has borrowed a hundred thousand, and we've secretly guaranteed it. A little delay in paying this allowance isn't unreasonable.” “Exactly. But drawing it from the treasury will take several months unless we work through the right connections.”

zh: 这是王有龄很明白的，领到公款，哪怕是十万火急的军饷，一样也要重重勒掯，尤其是藩司衙门的书办，格外难惹，“ ‘阎王好见，小鬼难当’！”他说，“麟藩台那里，我有把握，就是下面的书办，还想不出路子。”“我来！”胡雪岩想说：“你去见阎王，我来挡小鬼。”话到口边，想到“见阎王”三个字是忌讳，便不敢说俏皮话了，老老实实答道：“你那里备公事去催，下面我来想办法，大不了多花些小费就是了。“这样说停当，第二天王有龄就从海运局公款中，提了五千两银子，交结胡雪岩。钱是有了，但要事情办得顺利，还得有人，胡雪岩心里在盘算，如果光是开家钱庄，自己下手，一天到晚钉在店里，一时找不着好帮手也不碍。而现在的情形是，自己要在各方面调度，不能力日常的店面生意绊住身子，这就一定要托个能干而靠得住的人来做档手。
en: Wang understood that well. Even the most urgently needed military pay faced obstruction at every stage before release. The treasury clerks were particularly difficult. “‘The King of Hell is easy to see; his little demons are hard to manage!’” he said. “I can deal with Treasurer Lin, but I don't yet see a way through the clerks below him.” “Leave them to me.” Hu was about to say, “You go and see the King of Hell; I'll deal with the demons.” Then he remembered that telling someone to see the King of Hell was an ill-omened joke. He answered plainly instead. “Send an official document pressing for payment. I'll find a way among the subordinates. At worst, it will mean a little more in gratuities.” With that settled, Wang drew five thousand taels from the bureau's public funds the following day and handed it to Hu. The money was available, but smooth progress required people too. If Hu were merely opening a bank and could attend to it himself all day, the lack of a good assistant would not matter for the moment. But he had to coordinate matters in many directions and could not be tied down by daily business. He therefore needed a capable, trustworthy manager.

zh: 信和有两个过去的同事，倒是可造之材，不过他不愿去找他们，因为一则是挖了张胖子手下的“好角色”，同行的义气，个人的交情都不容出此，再则是自己的底细，那两个人十分清楚，原是玩笑惯的同事，一下子分成老板、伙计，自己抹不下这张脸，对方也难生敬畏之心。想来想去，想出来一个人，也是同行，但没有什么交情，这个人就在情和坊一家钱庄立柜台做伙计，胡雪岩跟他打过一次交道，觉得他头脑很清楚，仪表、口才也是庸中佼佼，大可以物色了来。这件事最好托张胖子。由此又想到一个难题，从在上海回杭州的船上，下决心开钱庄那一刻起，他就在考虑，这件事要不要先跟张胖子谈，还是等一切就绪，择吉开张的时候再告诉他？其实只要认真去想一想，胡雪岩立刻便会发觉，早告诉他不见得有好处，而迟告诉了必定有坏处，第一，显得不够交情，倒象是瞒着他什么，会引起他的怀疑，在眼前来说，张胖子替他和王有龄担着许多风险，诚信不孚，会惹起不痛快。而且招兵买马开一爿钱庄，也是瞒不住人的，等张胖子发觉了来问，就更加没意思了。
en: Two former colleagues at Xinhe had promise, but he did not want to approach them. First, he would be taking good men from Zhang. Neither the obligations of the trade nor their personal friendship permitted it. Second, they knew his background too well. They had joked together as equals. Suddenly becoming employer and employees would embarrass him and make it difficult for them to regard him with proper respect. After much thought, he remembered another man in the trade with whom he had little personal connection. He worked at the counter of a bank in Qinghefang. Hu had dealt with him once and found him clear-headed, with an appearance and manner of speaking well above the ordinary. He was worth recruiting. Zhang would be the best person to approach him. That brought up another problem. Ever since deciding to open a bank on the return voyage from Shanghai, Hu had wondered whether to tell Zhang first or wait until everything was ready and an auspicious opening date selected. A moment's serious thought made the answer plain. Early disclosure might bring no benefit, but late disclosure would certainly do harm. It would first suggest a lack of friendship, as though he were concealing something, and invite suspicion. Zhang was currently bearing substantial risks for him and Wang. Any loss of trust would cause trouble. Besides, gathering staff and opening a bank could not be kept secret. If Zhang discovered it and came to ask, the position would be more awkward still.

zh: 主意打定，特为到盐桥信和去看张胖子，相见欢然，在店里谈过一阵闲话，胡雪岩便说：“张先生，我有件要紧事跟你商量。”说着，望了望左右。“到里头来说。”张胖子把他引入自己的卧室，房间甚小，加上张胖子新从上海洋行里买回来的一具保险箱，越发显得狭隘，两个就坐在床上谈话。“张先生，我决什自己弄个号子。”“好啊！”张胖子说，声音中有些做作出来的高兴。胡雪岩明白，张胖子是怕他自设钱庄，影响信和的生意，关于海运局这方面的往来，自然要起变化了。因此他首先就作解释“你放心！‘兔子不吃窝边草’，要有这个心里，我也不会第一个就来告诉你。海运局的往来，照常归信和，我另打路子。”“噢！”张胖子问，“你是怎么打法？”“这要慢慢看。总而言之一句话，信和的路子，我一定让开。”“好的！”张胖子现在跟胡雪岩的情分关系不同了，所以不再说什么言不由衷的门面话，很坦率地答道“作为人我相信得过。你肯让一步，我见你的情，有什么忙好帮，只要我办得到，一定尽心尽力。你说！”
en: Having decided, Hu made a special visit to Xinhe at Salt Bridge. Their meeting was cordial. After chatting in the shop, he said, “Mr Zhang, I have something important to discuss,” and glanced around. “Come inside.” Zhang led him to his bedroom. It was small, and a safe recently purchased from a foreign firm in Shanghai made it more cramped still. They sat on the bed. “Mr Zhang, I've decided to establish a firm of my own.” “Excellent!” Zhang's pleasure sounded somewhat forced. Hu understood: he feared that Hu's bank would affect Xinhe's business. Its dealings with the Sea Transport Bureau were naturally likely to change. He therefore began with reassurance. “Don't worry. A rabbit doesn't eat the grass beside its own burrow. If I meant to take your business, I wouldn't be telling you first. The bureau's dealings will remain with Xinhe. I'll find a different path.” “Oh? What path?” “That will emerge in time. In short, whatever business Xinhe is pursuing, I'll keep clear of it.” “Good.” Their relationship had changed, and Zhang no longer offered insincere courtesies. He answered frankly. “I trust your character. If you're willing to make that concession, I appreciate it. Whatever help I can give, I'll give wholeheartedly. Tell me what you need.”

zh: “当然要请张先生帮忙。第一，开门那天，要捧捧我的场。”“那还用得着说？开门那天，我约同行来‘堆花’，多没有把握，万把两现银子，是有的。”“好极！我先谢谢。”胡雪岩说，“第二件，我立定宗旨，信和的好手，决不来挖。我现在看中一个人，想请张先生从中替我拉一拉。”“哪个？你说说看！”“清和坊大源，有个小朋友，好象姓刘，人生得蛮‘外场’的。我想约他出来谈一谈。““姓刘，蛮‘外场’的？”张胖子皱着眉想了一会想起来了，“你的眼光不错！不过大源的老板、档手，我都很熟，所以这件事我不便出面，我寻个人替他把他约出来见面，将来谈成了，你不可说破是我替你拉拢的！”
en: “Naturally, I must ask your help. First, support me on opening day.” “That goes without saying. I'll bring fellow bankers to make a show of deposits. I can't promise a great deal, but there'll be ten thousand taels or so in silver.” “Excellent. Thank you in advance. Second, I've made it a rule not to take any of Xinhe's good men. I've found someone else and would like you to help bring us together.” “Who?” “At Dayuan in Qinghefang there's a young fellow, surnamed Liu, I think. A presentable man who knows how to deal with people. I'd like to meet him.” “Liu? Presentable?” Zhang frowned in thought, then remembered. “You have a good eye. But I know both Dayuan's proprietor and its manager well, so I can't intervene openly. I'll have someone arrange a meeting. If it works out, you mustn't reveal that I brought you together.”

zh: “晓得，晓得。”张胖子没有说假话，他帮胡雪岩的忙，确是尽心尽力，当时就托人把姓刘的约好。这天晚上快到二更了，有人到胡家去敲门，胡雪岩提盏“油灯照”去开门，把灯提起来往来人脸上一点，正是那姓刘的。“胡先生，信和的张先生叫我来看你。”“不错，不错，请里面坐。”请进客厅，胡雪岩请教名字，姓刘的名叫刘庆生。他就称他“庆生兄”。“庆生兄府上哪里？”“余姚。”“噢，好地方，好地方。”胡雪岩很感兴趣地说，“我去过。”于是谈余姚的风物，由余姚谈到宁波，再谈回绍兴，海阔天空，滔滔不绝，把刘庆生弄得莫名其妙，好几次拉回正题，动问有何见教？而胡雪岩总是敷衍一句，又把话扯了开去，倒象是长夜无聊，有意找个人来听他讲《山海经》似地。
en: “I understand.” Zhang had not spoken idly. He did all he could to help and immediately asked someone to contact Liu. That night, close to the second watch, a visitor knocked at Hu's house. Hu took an oil lamp to the door and raised it towards the man's face. It was Liu. “Mr Hu, Mr Zhang of Xinhe asked me to call.” “Yes, indeed. Come inside.” Once they were in the reception room, Hu asked his full name. It was Liu Qingsheng, and Hu addressed him as “Brother Qingsheng.” “Where is your family home?” “Yuyao.” “Ah, a fine place! I've been there,” Hu said with interest. They discussed Yuyao's sights and customs, moved on to Ningbo, then back to Shaoxing. Hu spoke endlessly on every imaginable subject, bewildering Liu. Several times Liu tried to return to the purpose of the visit and asked how he could be of service. Hu always gave a brief, evasive answer and wandered off again, as though bored by the long night and wanting someone to listen to fantastic tales from the Classic of Mountains and Seas.

zh: 刘庆生的困惑越来越深，而且有些懊恼，但他也是极坚忍的性格，胡雪岩与王有龄的一番遇台，当事人都从不跟别人谈，但张胖子了解十之五、六，闲谈之中，加油加酱地渲染着，所以同行都知道胡雪岩是个神秘莫测的“大好佬”，刘庆生心里在想：“找我来，必有所为，倒偏要看看你说些什么？”就由于这一转念，他能够忍耐了。胡雪岩就是要考验他的耐性。空话说了一个钟头，刘庆生毫无愠色，认为满意，第一关，实在也是最难的一关，算是过去了。这才谈到刘庆生的本行。胡雪岩是此中好手，借闲谈作考问，出的题目都很难。刘庆生照实回答，大都不错，第二关又算过去了。
en: Liu grew increasingly puzzled and somewhat annoyed. But he too had great perseverance. Neither Hu nor Wang ever told others the story of their remarkable connection. Zhang, however, knew half or more of it and embellished it freely in conversation. Everyone in the trade therefore knew Hu as an unfathomable man of consequence. Liu thought, “He must have a reason for bringing me here. I mean to see what he has to say.” That decision enabled him to endure. Hu was testing precisely that patience. After an hour of empty talk, Liu showed no irritation. Satisfied, Hu considered the first test—and in truth the hardest—passed. Only then did he turn to banking. An expert himself, he disguised his examination as casual conversation and set difficult questions. Liu answered to the best of his knowledge, mostly correctly. The second test was passed as well.

zh: “庆生兄，”他又问，“钱庄这一行，我离开得久了，不晓得现在城里的同业，一共有多少家？”“ ‘大同行，八家，’小同行，就多了，一共有三十三家。”“噢！哪三十三家？”这下才显出刘庆生的本事，从上城数到下城，以兑换银子、铜钱为主的三十三家“小同行”的牌号，一口气报了出来，一个不缺。这份记性，连胡雪岩都自叹不如。
en: “Brother Qingsheng, I've been away from banking for some time. How many firms are there in the city now?” “Eight large banks. There are more of the smaller establishments: thirty-three altogether.” “Which thirty-three?” Now Liu's ability truly appeared. From the Upper City to the Lower, he named every one of the thirty-three smaller firms whose main business was exchanging silver and copper cash. He gave the names without a pause and missed none. Even Hu felt his own memory inferior.

zh: 到此地步，他差不多已决定要用此人了，但是还不肯明说出来，“宝眷在杭州？”他问。“都在余姚。”刘庆生答。“怎么不接出来呢？”“还没有力量接家眷。”“ 想来你已经讨亲了？”“是的。”刘庆生说，“伢儿都有两个了。”“府上还有些什么人？“爷娘都在堂。还有个兄弟，在蒙馆里读书。”“这样说，连你自己，一家七口，家累也够重了！”“是啊！所以不敢搬到杭州来。”刘庆生说，“在家乡总比较好寻生路。”
en: By now Hu had all but decided to employ him, though he would not yet say so. “Is your family in Hangzhou?” “They're all in Yuyao.” “Why don't you bring them here?” “I can't afford it yet.” “I take it you're married?” “Yes. I have two children.” “Who else is in your household?” “Both my parents are alive, and I have a younger brother at an elementary school.” “Then, including yourself, there are seven mouths to feed. That's quite a burden.” “Yes. That's why I don't dare bring them to Hangzhou. It's easier to manage in our home district.”

zh: “倘或说搬到杭州，一个月要多少开销？”胡雪岩说，“不是说过苦日子，起码吃饭嘛一荤一素，穿衣嘛一绸一布，就是老婆嘛，一正一副也不算过分。”刘庆生笑道：“胡先生在说笑话了。”“就当笑话讲好了。你说说看！”“照这样子说，一个月开销，十两银子怕都不够。”“这也不算多。”胡雪岩接着便说：“杭州城里钱庄的大同行，马上要变九家了。”“喔！”刘庆生很注意地问：“还有一家要开出来？”不错，马上要开出来。““叫啥字号，开在哪里？”“字号还没有定，也不知道开在哪里。”“这……这是怎么回事？”
en: “If you did move them here, what would the monthly expenses be?” Hu asked. “I don't mean a life of hardship. At least a meat dish and a vegetable dish at meals, silk as well as cotton clothes—even a wife and a concubine wouldn't be excessive.” Liu laughed. “You're joking, Mr Hu.” “Then treat it as a joke. Give me a figure.” “On that basis, even ten taels a month might not be enough.” “That isn't much.” Hu continued, “Hangzhou's eight large banks are about to become nine.” “Oh?” Liu asked attentively. “Another is opening?” “Yes, very soon.” “What's its name? Where will it be?” “The name hasn't been decided, nor the location.” “Then... what do you mean?”

zh: 胡雪岩不答他的话，“庆生兄，”他问：“如果这家钱庄请你去做档手，大源肯不肯放？”“什么？”刘庆生疑惑自己听错了，“胡先生请你再说一遍。”这一次听清楚了，却又有些不大相信，细看胡雪岩的脸色，不象是在开玩笑，才知道自己的运气来了。“大源没有不肯放的道理。我在那里，感情处得不错，倘或有这样的好机会，同事听了也高兴的。”“那好！我请你，我请你做这家新开钱庄的档手。”“是胡先生自己要开钱庄？”刘庆生略有些讶异。“老板不是我，也好算是我，总之，一切我都可以作主。庆生兄，你说一个月至少要十两银子的开销，一年就是一百二十两，这样，我送你二百两银子一年，年底另有花红。你看如何？”
en: Hu ignored the question. “Brother Qingsheng, if this bank asked you to be its manager, would Dayuan let you go?” “What?” Liu thought he had misheard. “Please say that again.” This time he heard clearly, but could scarcely believe it. Studying Hu's face and finding no sign of a joke, he realised that his opportunity had arrived. “Dayuan would have no reason to refuse. I've got on well with everyone there. If such an opportunity came, my colleagues would be pleased for me.” “Good. Then I invite you to manage this new bank.” “You're opening it yourself, Mr Hu?” Liu was slightly surprised. “The proprietor isn't me, though you could say that I am. In any case, I have full authority. You say your expenses would be at least ten taels a month, or a hundred and twenty a year. Here's my offer: two hundred taels a year, with a bonus at year's end. What do you think?”

zh: 这还有什么话说？但太慷慨了，却又有些令人不信。胡雪岩看他的神情，猜到他心里，告个便到里面取了五十两一锭的四锭银子出来，放在他面前。“这是今年四月到明年三月的，你先关了去。”“不要，不要！”刘庆生激动不已，吵架似的把银子在外推，“胡先生，你这样子待人，说实话，我听都没有听见过，铜钱银子用得完，大家是一颗心，胡先生你吩咐好了，怎么说怎么好！”他激动，胡雪岩却冷静，很恳切地说：“庆生兄，这二百两头，你今天一定要带回去。钱是人的胆，你有这二百两银子在手里，心思可以定了，脑筋也就活了，想个把主意，自然就会高明。”“不是这话，不是这话……”“你不必再客气了，是你分内应得之财，客气什么？你不肯收，我反倒不便说话了。”“好，好，这先不谈。谈正经！”
en: What more could he ask? Yet the generosity was so great that it was difficult to believe. Reading his expression, Hu understood. He excused himself, went inside, and returned with four ingots of fifty taels each, which he set before Liu. “This is for the year from this fourth month to the third month next year. Take it in advance.” “No, no!” Deeply moved, Liu pushed the silver away almost as though quarrelling. “Mr Hu, frankly, I've never even heard of anyone treating a man like this. Money can be spent, but our hearts are what matter. Just give me your instructions. Whatever you say, I'll do.” While Liu was agitated, Hu remained calm. He spoke earnestly. “Brother Qingsheng, you must take these two hundred taels today. Money gives a man confidence. With it in your hands, your mind will be settled and your thoughts more active. Any ideas you devise will naturally be better.” “That isn't what I mean...” “No more ceremony. It's money you're properly entitled to. Why refuse it? If you won't accept, I'll find it difficult to speak freely.” “Very well. Let us leave that for now and discuss the business.”

zh: “对啊，谈正经。”胡雪岩说，“你今天回去，最好就把在大源经手的事，料理料理清楚。第一桩要寻店面，房子要讲究、漂亮，出脚要方便，地点一定要在上城。寻‘瓦摇头’多看几处，或买或典，看定了来告诉我。”“是的。第二桩？”“第二桩要寻伙计，你看中了就好了。”“是。第三桩？”“以后无非装修门面，买木器之类，都是你办，我不管。”刘庆生想了想答道：“我晓得了！胡先生请你明天立个一千两的折子，把图章交给我，随时好支用。”“不错！你替我写张条子，给信和的张先生。请他垫支一千两，立个折子。”这又是考一考他的文墨。刘庆生倒也应付裕如，把条子写好，胡雪岩看过不错，便画了花押，连同那二百两现银，一起让刘庆生带了回去。
en: “Exactly. When you go back today, put the affairs you've handled at Dayuan in order. Our first task is to find premises. The building must be handsome and well appointed, with convenient access, and it must be in the Upper City. Ask the property brokers to show you several places. We can buy it outright or take it in pledge. Once you've chosen, tell me.” “Yes. The second task?” “Find employees. Choose whomever you think suitable.” “And the third?” “After that, it's decorating the premises, buying furniture, and so on. You handle it all. I won't interfere.” Liu considered. “I understand. Tomorrow, please open an account with a thousand taels available and give me the seal, so I can draw funds as required.” “Quite right. Write a note to Mr Zhang at Xinhe, asking him to advance a thousand taels and open the account.” This was another test, of his writing. Liu handled it easily. Hu read the note, approved it, added his written signature mark, and sent Liu away with both the note and the two hundred taels in silver.

zh: 刘庆生是就在这一夕谈中，完全为胡雪岩降服了。他本来一个人住在店里，这夜为了有许多事要筹划，特意到客栈去投宿，找了间清静客房，问柜上借了副笔砚，讨两张“尺白纸”，一个人在油灯下把自己该做的事，一条一条记下来。等到写完，鸡都叫了。和衣躺了一会，天亮起身，虽然睡得极少，却是人逢喜事精神爽，提了银包，直回大源。同事见他一夜不回来，都道他狎妓去了，纷纷拿他取笑。刘庆生的为人，内方外圆，笑笑不响，动手料理自己经手的帐目，一把算盘打得飞快，到日中都已结算清楚。吃过午饭，说要去收帐，出店去替胡雪岩办事。第一件就是寻房子，这要请教“瓦摇头”。到了“茶会”上寻着熟人，说了自己所要的房子的格局，附带有个条件，要在“钱庄”附近，替他租一所小小的住屋，刘庆生的打算是要把家眷接了来，住得离钱庄近了，随时可以到店里去照应。约定了听回话的时间，然后要去寻伙计，人来人往，总要有个起坐联络的地方，离开大源他得有个住处，好得手里有二百两银子在，刘庆生决定去借客栈，包了一座小院子，共有三个房间。论月计算。接着到“荐头行”去挑了个老实勤快的“打杂”，当天就叫他到客栈来上工。
en: In that single evening, Hu had completely won Liu over. Liu normally lived alone at the bank, but with so much to plan that night, he deliberately took a quiet room at an inn. He borrowed brush and inkstone from the desk, asked for two sheets of plain writing paper, and sat beneath an oil lamp listing everything he must do. The cocks were crowing by the time he finished. He lay down in his clothes for a little while and rose at daybreak. Though he had slept very little, good fortune gave him energy. Taking his silver, he went straight back to Dayuan. His colleagues, assuming that his night away had been spent with a courtesan, teased him. Liu was firm inwardly and accommodating in manner. He only smiled and began putting his accounts in order. His abacus clicked rapidly, and by noon everything was settled. After lunch, he said he was going to collect debts and went out to attend to Hu's business. First came the premises, for which he needed a property broker. At the brokers' customary teahouse meeting place, he found an acquaintance and described the layout required. He added one condition: a small residence must be rented near the bank. He intended to bring his family to Hangzhou and live close enough to attend to the business whenever needed. After arranging when to hear the broker's reply, he turned to recruiting staff. With people coming and going, he needed somewhere to meet them, and once he left Dayuan he would need lodging too. Fortunately, he had two hundred taels. He rented a small courtyard of three rooms at an inn by the month, then went to an employment agency and selected an honest, industrious general servant, who began work at the inn that day.

zh: 看看天快黑了，大源的档手孙德庆，已经回家。刘庆生办了四样很精致的水礼。 登门拜访。“噢！”孙德庆大惑不解，“无缘无故来送礼，这是啥缘故？”“我有件事，要请孙先生栽培……”“我晓得，我晓得！”孙德庆抢着道：“我已经跟东家说过了，一过了节就要加你工钱。你何必还要破费？庆生，争钱不容易，这份礼起码值四两银子，你两个月的工钱，何苦？”他完全弄错了！但这番好意，反使得刘庆生难以启齿，笑一笑答道：“看来我要替孙先生和老板赔不是了！”“怎么？”孙德庆一惊：“你闯了什么祸？是不是吃进了倒帐？”“不是！”他把随身所带的帐簿，往孙德庆面前一放“帐都结清楚了，没有一笔帐收不到的。孙先生，我要走了。”
en: By dusk, Dayuan's manager, Sun Deqing, had gone home. Liu prepared four carefully chosen gifts of fresh provisions and called on him. “Oh!” Sun was bewildered. “Gifts out of the blue? What's the occasion?” “There's something on which I must ask your help...” “I know!” Sun interrupted. “I've already spoken to the proprietor. You'll get a raise after the festival. Why spend money on presents? Qingsheng, money isn't easily earned. These must have cost at least four taels—two months of your wages. Why do it?” He had completely misunderstood. Yet his kindness made Liu's news harder to deliver. Smiling, Liu said, “It seems I owe both you and the proprietor an apology.” “What?” Sun was alarmed. “What trouble have you caused? Taken on a bad debt?” “No.” Liu placed the account book he had brought before him. “Everything is settled. There isn't a single uncollectable account. Mr Sun, I'm leaving.”

zh: “走到哪里去？”“说出来孙先生一定替我高兴，有个朋友要弄个号子，叫我去做档手。”“唷！恭喜，恭喜！”孙德庆换了副怀疑的面孔又说，“不过，你倒说说看，是怎么样一个朋友？何以事先一点风声都不露？”“我也是昨天才撞着这么个难得的机会。”刘庆生说：“有个人，孙先生总晓得：胡雪岩！”“是从前信和的那个胡雪岩？他是你的新东家？”听到“新东家”三字，可知孙德庆已经答应了，刘庆生宽心大放，笑嘻嘻地答道：“大概是的。”“这就不对了！东定就是东家，什么大概，小概？胡雪岩这个人，我也见过，眉毛一动，就是一计。我看……”孙德庆终于很率直地说了出来，“有点不大靠得住！”
en: “Going where?” “You'll be pleased for me when I tell you. A friend is opening a bank and wants me as manager.” “Congratulations!” Then Sun looked doubtful. “But tell me: what sort of friend? Why was there no hint of this beforehand?” “I only came upon this exceptional opportunity yesterday. You must know the man: Hu Xueyan.” “The Hu Xueyan formerly at Xinhe? He's your new employer?” Those words showed that Sun had accepted his departure. Greatly relieved, Liu smiled. “I suppose so.” “That's not right. An employer is an employer. What do you mean, ‘suppose’? I've met Hu too. Every movement of his eyebrows means another scheme. I think...” At last Sun said frankly, “He's not entirely dependable.”

zh: “靠得住。”刘庆生说，“真的靠不住，我再回来，孙先生象我的长辈一样，也不会笑我。”这两句话很动听，孙德庆点点头：“水往低处流，人往高处爬，你一出去就做档手，也是大源的面子，但愿不出笑话。如果真的靠不住，你千万要当心，早早滑脚，还是回大源来。”过去也有过虚设钱庄，吸进了存款，一倒了事的骗局。孙德庆“千万要当心”的警告，就是怕有此一着，将来“东家”逃走，做档手的要吃官司。这是决不会有的事，但说这话总是一番好意。刘庆生本来还想表示，等钱庄开出来，跟大源做个“联号”，现在当然也不必送这个秋彼。答应一声：“我一定听孙先生的话。”随后便告辞了。
en: “He is dependable. And if he really isn't, I'll come back. You're like an elder to me, Mr Sun. You wouldn't laugh at me.” These words pleased Sun, who nodded. “Water flows downwards, but a man seeks to rise. Going straight into a manager's position does Dayuan credit too. I only hope it doesn't become a laughing matter. If he proves unreliable, be very careful. Leave promptly and come back to us.” There had been fraudulent banks before: empty establishments that took deposits and then collapsed. That was the danger behind Sun's warning. If the proprietor fled, the manager would face legal proceedings. Nothing of the kind could happen here, Liu felt, but the warning was well meant. He had intended to suggest that the new bank establish an affiliation with Dayuan. Now there was no point in offering that overture. He answered, “I shall certainly heed your advice,” and took his leave.

zh: 离了孙家，来到胡家，他把这一天的经过，扼要报告了胡雪岩。听说他在客栈里包了一个院子，胡雪岩就知道他做事是放得开手的，原来还怕他拘谨，才具不够开展，现在连这最后一层顾虑也消除了。“好的，你尽管去做。该你做主的，尽管做主，不必问我。”“有件事，一家要胡先生自己做主。”刘庄生问道，“字号不知道定了没有？定了要请人去写，好做招牌。”“对，这倒是要紧的。不过，我也还要去请教高明，明天告诉你。”
en: From Sun's house he went to Hu's and briefly reported the day's activities. Hearing that he had rented a courtyard at an inn, Hu knew that he could act freely and decisively. He had previously feared that Liu might be too constrained to develop his abilities fully. That last doubt now disappeared. “Excellent. Go ahead. Decide anything within your authority without asking me.” “There is one thing you must decide yourself,” Liu said. “Have you settled on the firm's name? Once you have, we need someone to write it so the signboard can be made.” “Yes, that is important. But I too must consult someone wiser. I'll tell you tomorrow.”
